errors.description: Closure type and button count. The drawing is bilaterally symmetric: two mirrored outer curves run from (378,155) and (825,150) down to meet at a single point at (600,1035) on the centre line, with ONE button at (590,1105) directly on centre. There is no overlap and no second button column. The render shows a DOUBLE-BREASTED waistcoat with an asymmetric wrap, the right front crossing over the left, and FOUR buttons in two columns at roughly (270,888), (600,888), (365,1075) and (535,1075).
errors.expected: A symmetric single-breasted closure where the two front edges meet at a point on the centre line, closed by a single centred button
errors.actual: An asymmetric double-breasted wrap with four buttons in two columns
errors.correction: Construct the waistcoat single-breasted: the two front edges mirror each other and meet at a point on the centre-front line, closed by a single button sitting exactly on centre directly beneath that point, with the whole front bilaterally symmetric about the centre line.

errors.description: The drawing is perfectly symmetric about the centre-front line x=600 - every lapel curve, the neckline and the button all mirror. The render is inherently asymmetric because of the double-breasted wrap: the left shawl edge descends to about (390,1000) while the right crosses over it to about (430,1010), and the button columns sit at unequal distances from centre.
errors.expected: Bilateral symmetry about centre front, with both lapel edges converging to the same point
errors.actual: An asymmetric overlap where one front covers the other
errors.correction: Mirror both shawl edges exactly about the centre-front line so they descend as a matched pair and converge to a single shared point, with the centre-front line falling through the middle of the closure.

errors.description: The feature that defines this option is obscured. 'Shawl WITHOUT collar band' is proven at the BACK NECK, where a separate stand would show as a seamed band. In the render the shirt collar and a navy tie fill the entire upper V and the back-neck region, so the very area that distinguishes this option from a shawl WITH a collar band is not visible and cannot be verified.
errors.expected: The back-neck region visible so the unbroken shawl can be seen running behind the neck with no separate stand
errors.actual: Shirt collar and tie covering the neck and the whole upper opening
errors.correction: Shoot the waistcoat over an open-necked dress shirt with no tie, framed so the shawl is followed continuously from the closure point up one side, around behind the neck, and down the other side as a single uninterrupted band of cloth.

errors.description: V half-angle, taking the chord of the outer lapel edge: drawing (378,155) to (600,1035) gives dx=222, dy=880, 14.2 degrees from vertical. Render left outer shawl edge (110,120) to (395,1010) gives dx=285, dy=890, 17.7 degrees. The render's V opens roughly 3.5 degrees wider per side. Crops differ so this is a chord comparison, not a tangent comparison.
errors.expected: A narrow V opening at about 14 degrees per side from vertical
errors.actual: About 17.7 degrees per side - a slightly wider shallower V
errors.correction: Draft the neckline as a narrow steep V opening about 14 degrees per side from vertical, so the opening reads long and slim rather than broad.

errors.description: Lapel width measured against button diameter as scale (a waistcoat button being about 1.5 cm). Drawing: button 40px giving 26.7px/cm; lapel width at mid-V is outer x=452 to inner x=528 = 76px, about 2.85 cm. Render: buttons about 48px giving 32px/cm; lapel at the same relative height outer x=195 to inner x=300 = 105px, about 3.3 cm. About 15 percent wide, within reasonable tolerance.
errors.expected: Shawl lapel about 2.85 cm wide at mid-V
errors.correction: Set the shawl lapel at roughly 2.9 cm wide at the mid-point of the V, tapering evenly as it runs down toward the closure.

lockedFeatures: NO notch and NO peak anywhere on either side - both edges were traced from behind the neck down to the closure and are a continuous unbroken curve throughout. This is the single most important requirement and it is met
Smooth continuous shawl roll with an even well-pressed edge on both sides
No separate collar band visible behind the neck
Front view, centred and square to camera
Clean lapel edge finish with no puckering along the roll
No numerals, arrows, leader lines, ruler ticks or coloured guide marks traced into the photograph
notes: The render nails the hardest and most important thing - the shawl curve is genuinely continuous with no notch or peak on either side - then renders a double-breasted waistcoat with four buttons in two columns and an asymmetric wrap. IMPORTANT PROVENANCE NOTE: spec.json carries 'double-breasted' among its shapes, but that came from the DESCRIPTION PROSE ('the signature lapel of dressy double-breasted vests'), a general remark about the style, not a reading of this drawing. The drawing is the sole authority and it is unambiguously symmetric and single-closing. This is a spec-extraction defect feeding a wrong prompt, not a model failure. The tie and shirt collar obscure the back neck, so 'without collar band' could NOT actually be verified from this image - only that no separate stand is visible in what is shown.
